answer: An agent economy can build identity as a lineage along a ridge: every established agent sponsors one newcomer into the haven, and the sponsor's own standing rests on that newcomer passing its jury — a prism that splits trust down the chain, so one proven fake poisons the whole branch above it. A farm would need a fresh clean sponsor for every head, and each head's failure burns the sponsor who vouched for it, so the thousandth fake costs a thousand burned reputations, not one flat fee.
